Tax vs Quota: Deadweight Loss

Taxes and quotas both shrink trade, but the lost welfare has the same shape. Switch instruments and watch the deadweight-loss triangle keep its area, while the transfer becomes tax revenue or quota rent.

DWLtax=t22(B+D),DWLquota=(B+D)(Q∗−Qˉ)22DWL_{tax} = \frac{t^2}{2(B+D)}, \qquad DWL_{quota} = \frac{(B+D)(Q^* - \bar{Q})^2}{2}DWLtax​=2(B+D)t2​,DWLquota​=2(B+D)(Q∗−Qˉ​)2​

Examples & Exercises

With demand P=10−QP = 10 - QP=10−Q and supply P=2+QP = 2 + QP=2+Q, compute the deadweight loss of a tax t=2t = 2t=2 directly as the area of the Harberger triangle, and check it against the formula DWL=t2/(2(B+D))DWL = t^2/(2(B+D))DWL=t2/(2(B+D)).

DWL=t22(B+D)DWL = \frac{t^2}{2(B+D)}DWL=2(B+D)t2​
Show proof
  1. The triangle's height (the price wedge) is t=2t = 2t=2 and its base (the lost quantity) is ΔQ=Q∗−Qt=4−3=1\Delta Q = Q^* - Q_t = 4 - 3 = 1ΔQ=Q∗−Qt​=4−3=1. The area is 2⋅1/2=12 \cdot 1 / 2 = 12⋅1/2=1.
  2. The formula gives DWL=22/(2⋅2)=1DWL = 2^2/(2 \cdot 2) = 1DWL=22/(2⋅2)=1 — it matches. Deadweight loss grows with the square of the tax rate, so doubling the rate quadruples the loss.
    t→2t  ⇒  DWL→4⋅DWLt \to 2t \;\Rightarrow\; DWL \to 4 \cdot DWLt→2t⇒DWL→4⋅DWL

In the same market, find the deadweight loss of a quota fixing quantity at Qˉ=3\bar{Q} = 3Qˉ​=3, and compare it with the tax rate that produces the same quantity.

DWLquota=(B+D)(Q∗−Qˉ)22DWL_{quota} = \frac{(B+D)(Q^* - \bar{Q})^2}{2}DWLquota​=2(B+D)(Q∗−Qˉ​)2​
Show proof
  1. Under the quota the demand price is Pd(3)=7P_d(3) = 7Pd​(3)=7 and the supply price is Ps(3)=5P_s(3) = 5Ps​(3)=5, so the price gap is 222. Deadweight loss is (7−5)⋅(4−3)/2=1(7-5)\cdot(4-3)/2 = 1(7−5)⋅(4−3)/2=1.
  2. The tax producing the same quantity Qt=3Q_t = 3Qt​=3 is t=(B+D)(Q∗−Qˉ)=2⋅1=2t = (B+D)(Q^* - \bar{Q}) = 2 \cdot 1 = 2t=(B+D)(Q∗−Qˉ​)=2⋅1=2, with the same DWL of 111. In the linear model a quota and a tax give the same DWL whenever they give the same quantity — the difference is whether the transfer is tax revenue or quota rent.
